title: Brief to pipeline
scenario:
A juice brand wants a vertical ad. You are choosing how to build it. The brief, the recipe facts and a draft pipeline sheet are in the exhibit.

The brief and the draft sheet are made up for this case. The recipe facts are from Runway's docs.
exhibit:
Client brief (made up for this case)
  Deliverable: 10-second vertical ad (9:16) for a juice bottle
  Sound: none. The client adds its own music.
  Inputs: 3 product photos. One photo has a stock-site watermark in the corner.
  Also: the client's own chat assistant should make a banner whenever a
        user asks for one, in the same conversation.

Recipe facts (from Runway's docs)
  Product Ad:        1-10 product images, up to 4 style images.
                     Length 4-15 s, default 10. Audio default: false.
                     Reference guidelines: avoid watermarks or overlaid
                     text on product images.
  Multi-Shot Video:  mode auto (one story prompt) or custom (3-5 shots,
                     shot lengths must add up to the total).
                     Total length 5, 10 or 15 s. Audio default: true.
  Version:           use a dated version (for example 2026-06) to pin
                     behavior, or unsafe-latest to track the newest stable.

OpenAI (from the docs)
  image_generation tool: when included in a request, the model can
  decide when and how to generate images as part of the conversation.
  The result comes back as a base64-encoded image.

Draft pipeline sheet (made up for this case)
  Step              Person checks        Saved where
  1 Clean photos    designer             project folder
  2 Make video      art director         project folder
  3 Send to client  -                    email

questions.prompt: A teammate picks Multi-Shot Video and leaves the audio setting unset. What is the risk?

options.text: The video will be silent, because Runway never makes sound in its recipes.
options.explanation: Runway's pages list an audio setting for recipes, and Multi-Shot Video defaults it to true.

options.text: The recipe will refuse to run until you give it an audio value, and return an error.
options.explanation: The docs list audio as optional, with a default.

options.text: Audio defaults to true, so the video may have sound though the brief says none.
options.explanation: Right. Runway's Multi-Shot Video page lists audio as true by default. Product Ad's default is false. Always check each recipe's defaults.

options.text: The length will be cut to 5 seconds, because sound takes up some of the time.
options.explanation: Audio does not change the length. The total length is its own setting.

questions.prompt: One product photo has a stock-site watermark. What is the best step?

options.text: Use it as a style image instead of a product image.
options.explanation: Style images define lighting, palette and mood. A watermark does not become safe there.

options.text: Keep the photo and write in the prompt that the watermark should be ignored.
options.explanation: Runway's guidelines say to avoid watermarks in the inputs. They do not suggest asking the model to ignore them.

options.text: Replace it with a clean photo, or remove the watermark, before submitting.
options.explanation: Right. Runway's reference guidelines say to avoid watermarks or overlaid text on product images. It also lists such text as a cause of failed generations.

options.text: Submit it as it is. The recipe will ignore the watermark.
options.explanation: Runway's guidelines say to avoid watermarks. It does not say they are ignored.

questions.prompt: The client's chat assistant should make a banner when a user asks. Which prebuilt option fits best?

options.text: Add OpenAI's built-in image generation tool to the chat request, and the model decides when.
options.explanation: Right. The tool page says the model can decide when and how to generate images as part of the conversation. You do not build the image step.

options.text: Use Runway's Product Ad recipe for each chat message, so every banner is one task.
options.explanation: Product Ad turns product photos into a short video through one task. It is not a tool the chat model calls during a conversation.

options.text: Use Runway's Multi-Shot Video recipe, because the chat makes several images that can be joined into one video.
options.explanation: Multi-Shot Video builds a video from shots. The request here is for images inside a chat.

options.text: Build a three-tool chain of your own first, with a step for each task in the flow.
options.explanation: A chain of your own gives control but costs build time. A built-in tool already covers a single image step in a chat.

questions.prompt: Look at the draft pipeline sheet. What gap would you fix first?

options.text: Add a person check to step 3, before the client gets anything.
options.explanation: Right. This is our rule: keep a person at every client-facing step. Step 3 sends the ad out with no check.

options.text: Remove step 1, because recipes clean photos by themselves.
options.explanation: The Runway docs say strong references are the biggest lever on quality. They do not say recipes clean them.

options.text: Replace the "saved where" column with the vendor's task link.
options.explanation: Runway's primer says output URLs are temporary. Saving the file in your own place is the safer record.

options.text: Add a fourth step to run the video twice for safety, then keep both files.
options.explanation: A second run does not add a check. It adds cost and an extra file.

questions.prompt: Later the client asks for this flow: three still styles, an art director picks one, then a clip that starts from the chosen still and ends on a packshot. Which level fits?

options.text: Product Ad, because it is built for product videos and takes up to 10 images.
options.explanation: Product Ad fits a plain product ad in one call. It does not offer a human pick in the middle.

options.text: A single call, because it is one video in the end and the client wants it fast.
options.explanation: The flow has three stages and a person decision. A single call does not cover them.

options.text: A vendor recipe, because it picks the best of the three stills for the art director.
options.explanation: A recipe runs its own set steps. Neither recipe in the exhibit lets an art director pick one still in the middle.

options.text: Your own chain with the director's pick as a person step, as Veo allows first and last frames.
options.explanation: Right. A recipe wraps its own steps. This flow has a human choice in the middle, so you chain the steps yourself. The Gemini API docs say Veo 3.1 can use first and last frames.
